title: Don't drink the first glass of tap water in the morning.
accent: Let the tap run for a bit first.

title: The water sat in the pipes all night
body: When a tap isn't used for 6+ hours, the water just sits still in the pipes and the faucet.
Meanwhile, metal from old pipes, solder joints and brass faucet parts can dissolve into it.
The longer it sits, the more builds up.

title: Until it's as cold as it gets
body: If someone just showered or flushed the toilet: 5–30 seconds is enough.
If no water has been used: 2 minutes or longer.
The sign is simple: when your hand feels the water turn cold, you're done.

title: Hot tap water is for washing only
body: For tea, cooking and especially baby formula, use the cold tap only.
Hot water dissolves metal from pipes faster, so it tends to carry more lead.
Fill the kettle with cold water and boil it. It takes a minute or two longer, that's all.

title: Boiling doesn't remove lead
body: Boiling kills germs, but it doesn't get rid of metals.
As water evaporates, the share of metal actually goes up a little.
So start clean: with cold, flushed water.

title: Babies
body: US EPA estimate: formula-fed infants can get 40–60% of their lead exposure from water.
A child's body absorbs more metal than an adult's.

title: What else do you want to know about water?
accent: Tell me in the comments. The next post will be about it.
